text:
Alex: Quick question — thinking about route hierarchy for the API gateway. We currently match by path + header fallback. What's the behavior when both route-level model_pin and a client header alias are present? Should header override or should the route pin take precedence?

Priya: I lean route pin takes precedence for safety. Route configs are set by product/platform to guarantee compat. Header override is too permissive by default.

Oliver: Right now the code favors header because it’s more specific to the request. That was intentional early on but it might be causing surprises. :shrug:

Mia: From infra/ops POV header-winning causes noisy telemetry and makes quota/billing attribution messy. We also see spike patterns when SDKs send headers for experiments.

Alex: Proposed rule: explicit route config (model_pin) wins. Introduce a per-route flag `allow_header_override` which defaults to `false`. If true, header alias can override.

Kevin: Also important: compatibility checks. If the header alias resolves to a model version that is incompatible with route constraints (e.g., different tokenizer, incompatible KV cache layout), we must reject with a 412 and no fallback. Silent execution with mismatched model can corrupt results.

Priya: +1 for 412. Also add clear telemetry tags: `routing_decision=route_pin|header_override|alias_resolution` so we can query how often overrides happen.

Oliver: Console UX idea: show per-route "Allow header overrides" toggle and a live table of recent header override attempts with success/fail counts and reasons. That will help product teams understand impact.

route-bot: deploy-plan created: "routing-defaults-v2" — staging canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%. See: https://ci.redwood/internal/plans/1423

Mia: Quota implications: header override may resolve to premium/dedicated-only models. Routes should be able to specify `model_tier_whitelist` or deny premium aliases for public routes. Otherwise a user could bump into dedicated capacity and error.

Alex: Implementation sketch: matcher order becomes — (1) explicit `model_pin` on route, (2) route-level default alias, (3) header alias if `allow_header_override` is true. If alias resolves to a model that violates route constraints (compat flags, tier whitelist), return 412 or 403 as appropriate.

Kevin: We can reuse the model metadata service to check compatibility. It exposes `compatibility_flags` like ["kv-cache-v2","tok-v1","max-seq-8k"]. Routes will declare required flags and forbidden flags.

Priya: Console should warn when you try to pin an alias that doesn't meet the route's required flags. Prevents accidental misconfiguration at creation time.

Oliver: Edge-case: clients might send both header alias and a `model_version` param in the request body. Which wins? My suggestion: only honor header override (if allowed). Body-level version params should be ignored unless the request is authenticated as a service account owner of the route. Simpler for now: ignore body param and log the attempt.

Alex: Tests: unit tests for precedence rules, e2e for canary rollout and telemetry tagging. Also add integration tests where header asks for incompatible alias -> expect 412.

Mia: Ops TODOs: maintain fallback list per-route (explicit fallbacks) rather than auto-picking a cheaper alias. That avoids silent quality regressions. Also add a dashboard: per-route override rate, override failure reasons, top alias requests, and billing attribution by routing_decision.

Kevin: I'll open a PR with code + migration to add `allow_header_override` and route `compat_flags`. Will add telemetry emit points.

Priya: Thanks. Also we should throttle header-override attempts per-client to avoid abuse; maybe 10/min by default.

Oliver: Agree. Can we schedule a short sync tomorrow 10am to finalize UX/metrics?

Alex: Yup — 10am works. Thanks everyone.
